learningObjectives: Differentiate inhibition, updating, shifting, planning and monitoring.
Identify major cortical and subcortical control systems.
Explain why executive performance varies across contexts.
Translate executive mechanisms into practical environmental supports.

anatomy.label: Lateral prefrontal cortex
anatomy.detail: Lateral PFC sustains goals and relational structure across delays.
anatomy.clinical: Dysfunction may produce distractibility, poor planning and reduced cognitive flexibility.

anatomy.label: Posterior parietal cortex
anatomy.detail: Parietal systems allocate attention and maintain action-relevant representations.
anatomy.clinical: Disruption can impair working memory, selection and goal-directed attention.

anatomy.label: Dorsal anterior cingulate
anatomy.detail: dACC signals when control demands or errors require adjustment.
anatomy.clinical: Altered monitoring can contribute to perseveration or inefficient overcontrol.

anatomy.label: Basal-ganglia gating
anatomy.short: Update working memory and action policies
anatomy.detail: Corticostriatal loops regulate when representations and actions are opened or suppressed.
anatomy.clinical: Dopaminergic imbalance can alter effort, flexibility and response vigour.

anatomy.label: Control-network coordination
anatomy.detail: Frontoparietal and cingulo-opercular networks adapt connectivity to current goals.
anatomy.clinical: Poor coordination may appear as inconsistency rather than global impairment.

interaction.title: Explore the Executive Function
interaction.instruction: Select a component, then run the sequence.

stages.label: Goal
stages.text: Represent the desired outcome and task rules.

stages.label: Gate
stages.text: Permit useful information or actions while suppressing competitors.

stages.label: Monitor
stages.text: Compare performance with the goal and detect conflict or error.

stages.label: Adapt
stages.text: Shift strategy, effort or environment when the current plan is ineffective.

quizBank.question: Executive function is best understood as:
options: A family of interacting control processes
A single ability located in one frontal spot
quizBank.explanation: Executive control includes separable but interacting processes distributed across networks.

quizBank.question: Dorsal anterior cingulate cortex contributes strongly to:
quizBank.explanation: dACC tracks conflict, errors, effort and the need for control adjustment.

quizBank.question: Basal-ganglia gating helps regulate:
options: What enters working memory and which actions are selected
quizBank.explanation: Corticostriatal loops regulate updating and action selection.

quizBank.question: Which factor can reduce executive performance without permanent frontal damage?
quizBank.explanation: Fatigue and sleep loss can substantially impair attention, inhibition and working memory.

quizBank.question: The most accurate clinical statement is:
options: Executive performance depends strongly on context and scaffolding
Normal testing rules out daily impairment
quizBank.explanation: Structured testing may reduce real-world demands; context and supports materially affect performance.

prompts: Name the major components of the Executive Function.
Explain one clinically relevant function of the Executive Function.
Identify one common oversimplification to avoid.
